title: Reported child-care work-time loss varies by resource endpoint within a selected care-prevention universe
source_unit: identified SIPP reference-parent person-month record with EWORKMORE=1 and valid ETIMELOST

denominator.unit: valid selected reference-parent person records with valid reported time-loss amount

observations.method: Conditional descriptive mean and type shares using WPFINWGT and all 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: The estimate conditions on valid EWORKMORE=1 and ATIMELOST responses; it is not a population care-burden estimate. The fall-reference-year time-loss measure is attached to a SIPP person-month record.
observations.subgroup: Reference parents below 1x poverty with child-care arrangements reported to prevent working or working more and a valid time-loss amount.
observations.counterinterpretation: Resource endpoint may be associated with job schedule, care arrangement, reporting unit, ability to avoid time loss, and selection into the reference-parent universe; it does not show resources caused the amount.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; 4x poverty or more endpoint

denominator.unit: valid selected reference-parent person records with valid reported time-loss amount

observations.method: Conditional descriptive mean and type shares using WPFINWGT and all 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: The estimate conditions on valid EWORKMORE=1 and ATIMELOST responses; the high-resource point estimate has a wide interval and should not be ranked as a stable burden difference. The fall-reference-year time-loss measure is attached to a SIPP person-month record.
observations.subgroup: Reference parents at 4x poverty or more with child-care arrangements reported to prevent working or working more and a valid time-loss amount.
observations.counterinterpretation: The higher reported mean may reflect reporting in hours rather than days or weeks, job and care arrangements, schedule flexibility, and selection; it is not evidence of greater care burden.

related_sources.claim: Reader-facing interpretation of the conditional time-loss amount and its timing boundary.
Official definitions and universes for EWORKMORE, ETIMELOST, and time-loss type fields.

reproduction_audit.result: The committed conditional means and time-loss type shares reproduce the v18 local output for both displayed resource endpoints.
reproduction_audit.interpretation: Reproduction confirms a descriptive conditional layer, not a causal care, resource, earnings, recovery, trust, or political-action estimate. Raw inputs remain outside the repository.

boundary: This record measures reported child-care-related work-time loss only after work prevention and valid time-loss response gates. It does not establish a dated bill or provider event, actual care minutes, schedule control, earnings effect, protected or sacrificed household outcome, recovery, remedy, trust, political action, or exit.
